sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Deep-Sea Tugboat Towage and Maritime Emergency Salvage Contracts

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary national system, French-inspired commercial law tradition, with EU law primacy; no sub-state tax distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (freedom of establishment and free movement of capital; EU/EAA legal framework)
Luxembourg–United States Double Taxation Convention, signed 3 April 1996, as amended by the 2009 Protocol
Luxembourg–Germany Double Taxation Agreement (2012, as amended)

OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters and Multilateral Instrument for BEPS; bilateral investment treaty coverage depends on the home-state investment treaty network applicable to the ultimate beneficial owner

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as consolidated (SARL provisions, Articles 710-1 et seq.); Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended, including by the Law of 25 July 2023; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners, as amended; implementing Grand-Ducal Regulation of 20 January 2020; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Societies; EU Anti-Money-Laundering Directives and applicable EU restrictive-measures regulations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified extract from the trade/companies register or certificate of good standing of each direct corporate shareholder owning 25% or more of the SARL; if a corporate shareholder is newly formed, a notarized certificate of registration of its incorporating deed.
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies register or trade registry of the shareholder's place of incorporation; for Luxembourg shareholders, Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the state of origin if a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; otherwise consular legalization by the Luxembourg diplomatic or consular post with jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity document of each individual UBO owning 25% or more and of each proposed SARL manager, with notarial certification of the signature and identity.
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent passport-issuing authority in the UBO's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille of the notarial certification, or consular legalization if the country is not an Apostille Convention member; where the UBO appears before a Luxembourg notary, original documents may be verified without foreign apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of tax residence or tax domicile of each corporate UBO and each intermediate holding entity in the ownership chain.
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Revenue or tax authority of the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; for EU/EEA jurisdictions a self-certified tax residence statement may supplement but does not replace the certified certificate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the Luxembourg notary or incorporation agent to execute the incorporation application, make the name reservation, and file the UBO declaration.
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of signature or a Luxembourg notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization if executed abroad; if signed before a Luxembourg notary, no apostille is required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and documentary source-of-funds evidence for the proposed initial capital contribution, certified by the issuing bank or financial institution.
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank or financial institution maintaining the funding account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization where required by the receiving bank or notary's internal verification policy; otherwise bank-confirmed signature under the relevant banking standards

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all identified UBOs, managers, attorneys-in-fact, and material counterparties of the towage/salvage entity against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions lists, Luxembourg competent-authority freezing and blocking lists, the OFAC SDN List for USD-cleared payments, and public PEP databases such as World-Check/Refinitiv or comparable systems. The AML/CFT policy must document the risk rating, verify corporate and individual UBO identity before incorporation, obtain source-of-funds evidence for the capital contribution, perform adverse-media checks, require senior-management approval for PEP relationships, screen on an ongoing basis, and retain all records for at least five years. Because ISIC 5222 maritime towage and salvage is classified as Medium-Risk Enhanced, the SARL should appoint a responsible person for AML/CFT internal controls and implement a written CDD procedure before opening bank accounts or executing Lloyd's Standard Form contracts.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); online official portal at https://www.lbr.lu and https://www.rcsl.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal form suffix must appear in French as 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or 'SARL'. The name may be in French, German, Luxembourgish, English, or another language using the Latin alphabet; non-Latin names must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet. The constitutive deed must be drawn in French or German, and a certified translation is required when executed in another language.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words suggesting banking, credit, payment, insurance, reinsurance, investment-fund, stock-exchange, clearing-house, or central-securities-depository activity, such as 'banque', 'bancaire', 'assurance', 'réassurance', 'fonds', 'OPCVM', 'SICAV', 'SICAF', 'bourse', or 'clearing', without prior CSSF or CAA authorization

Words suggesting state, government, public administration, or official institutions, such as 'Etat', 'gouvernement', 'administration publique', 'commune', 'national', 'chambre de commerce', 'barreau', or 'université', without ministerial, institutional, or statutory approval

Words implying official maritime licensing or flag-state authority, such as 'registre maritime', 'administration des affaires maritimes', 'port authority', 'flag state', or 'official salvage service', without prior authorization from the Luxembourg Shipping Registry or the Administration de la navigation
Names identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered or reserved company name, and names contrary to Luxembourg public policy or good morals
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name reservation is submitted electronically through the LBR/RCS portal before the deed is signed. A successful reservation is valid for 60 calendar days and may be renewed by written request for one further 60-day period before expiry. If the RCS rejects the name, the applicant may request a written statement of grounds within 15 days of the refusal, submit a revised name with a new reservation request, or file an administrative appeal before the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within one month of the notification of the final refusal. A Luxembourg avocat must be engaged for the formal administrative appeal, and it is recommended to challenge any refusal first via the RCS review procedure before filing the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or registered-only office is permitted only for initial correspondence and address purposes, provided the SARL uses a licensed domiciliation agent in Luxembourg. For an ISIC 5222 marine towage and emergency salvage operation, the Luxembourg tax and maritime administration authorities will require substantive commercial presence, including a real operational office, local management, books and records, dispatch capability, crew/vessel administration, and insurance oversight. A purely virtual office is not acceptable for establishing tax residence or obtaining maritime operational substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-to-high. Quantified probability: 35-50% within the first 36 months of operation. Unannounced inspections may be carried out by the RCS, the Administration de l'enregistrement, the Luxembourg direct tax administration, the maritime administration, and AML/CFT supervisory authorities because ISIC 5222 towage and salvage is classified as Medium-Risk Enhanced and involves cross-border wire and escrow settlement.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official name pre-reservation and LBR/RCS name-check application fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official LBR tariff for electronic name reservation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial authentication of articles of association and lodging of incorporation deed for SARL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff for SARL formation plus disbursements; prevailing market range EUR 1,200-1,600

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS company registration and mandatory publication in RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / RCS; Ministry of Justice RESA

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO (RBE) initial declaration and filing-agent due-diligence fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RCS/LBR official declaration is free of charge; amount covers licensed preparing agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market agent fee for electronic submission, verification, and UBO register compliance

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Title II, Chapter 2 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée, Articles 100-1 to 100-34); Law of 19 December 1988 on the commercial register; Grand-Ducal Regulation on the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) of Luxembourg District Court
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte de société) executed before a Luxembourg notary, filed with the RCS and published in RESA
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SARL must have a minimum issued share capital of EUR 12,000. All shares must be fully subscribed and paid up at incorporation. Cash contributions must be remitted to a blocked escrow account opened in the name of the proposed company with a Luxembourg credit institution or to the notary's client account, with a bank confirmation certificate delivered to the notary. Non-cash contributions require a report by an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: THAT the Subscribers hereby subscribe for 120 ordinary shares of EUR 100 each in the capital of LU_SARL, and the full amount of EUR 12,000 is paid up through deposit into the designated blocked escrow account. RESOLVED FURTHER: THAT the registered office be adopted as 12 Rue du Parc, L-2345 Luxembourg. RESOLVED FURTHER: THAT [FULL_NAME] is appointed as sole manager (gérant) with all legal powers, and [NAME_A] and [NAME_B] as bank co-signatories. RESOLVED FINALLY: THAT the manager is authorised to make RCS registration, RESA publication, VAT, business licence filings, and to engage advisers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Governance and Dossier Compliance Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notarial office and legal counsel; statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) for non-cash considerations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Legal counsel confirms that the proposed corporate purpose for offshore towage and maritime salvage is lawful under Luxembourg law and compatible with SARL provisions. Draft articles of association are prepared, beneficial ownership information is documented, and the dossier is submitted to the notary for preliminary review before signature.
required_dossiers: Group structure chart and beneficial ownership statement
Consent forms from proposed shareholders and managers
Lease or letter of comfort for the registered office
KYC / ID copies for all individuals involved
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the lawfulness of offshore towage and salvage activities, file a supporting memorandum with P&I club membership and obtain a maritime-law opinion; revise the corporate purpose to include necessary ancillary activities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked Capital Escrow and Bank Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution authorised by the CSSF; notary's client account if used
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the future name of LU_SARL and deposit the full EUR 12,000 capital. Request an unqualified bank confirmation letter (attestation bancaire) stating that the funds are reserved for the company and may only be released upon registration of the SARL. Deliver such letter to the notary.
required_dossiers: Bank KYC forms for the proposed company
Declaration and source of funds documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue the blocked capital attestation, use the notary's escrow arrangement (compte séquestre) and obtain an equivalent certification from the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Notarial Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary acting under the authority of the Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All subscribers, or their duly constituted attorneys-in-fact, appear before the notary to sign the deed of incorporation and the articles of association. The notary verifies the identity and legal capacity of the signatories, confirms payment of the subscribed capital, and delivers a certified deed for RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Original passports or official identity documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If execution is rejected for incomplete corporate consents or signature defects, schedule an immediate second notarial appointment and re-execute the deed after correcting the formal deficiencies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) of Luxembourg District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the certified deed, statutory details of the managers, share capital information, and corporate purpose via the e-RCS electronic portal. The applicable RCS filing fee is paid and the company receives its RCS extract and registration number.
required_dossiers: Consent of managers to act as officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the filing for missing purpose descriptions or manager consents, submit a rectification deed or explanatory note through e-RCS within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Electronic Official Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA) via Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the certified incorporation notice and legal particulars with RESA through the LBR platform. Confirm the RESA publication date, which triggers legal effectiveness against third parties under Luxembourg law.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial deed
List of managers and registered office address
Proof of RCS filing fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA issues a non-conformity notice due to inconsistencies in the deed extract, coordinate with the registry and the notary, obtain a corrected publication text, and re-file through the same portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy — Directorate for Small and Medium Enterprises (Direction des Classes Moyennes)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, apply for the autorisation d'établissement through MyGuichet.lu under the Luxembourg Law of 2 September 2011 on the freedom of establishment. Provide certified copies of incorporation documents, proof of professional good conduct for managers, the lease of the registered office, and evidence of liability insurance for the proposed towage and salvage undertakings.
required_dossiers: Criminal record excerpt (casier judiciaire) for each manager
Civil liability and P&I insurance certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the establishment permit is refused on professional reliability grounds, submit a formal reassessment request to the Ministry of the Economy with supplementary compliance documentation and external advisory support, and appeal if necessary under the administrative law procedures.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy — Industrial Establishments Division (Postes et Installations) in conjunction with the Luxembourg Maritime Administration for vessel-related operations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (commercial operating permit) for the exercise of ISIC 5222 activities; additional Luxembourg maritime certificate of registry is required for any vessel to be operated under the Luxembourg flag

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C — environmental declaration only for head-office and administrative functions; Category B preliminary EIA assessment and permit if a shore-based workshop, winching yard, or vessel maintenance facility is established in Luxembourg
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater from the registered office. If shore facilities are developed, wastewater discharges must comply with Luxembourg Water Law limits for oil, grease, and heavy metals. VOC emissions are subject to EU Directive 2010/75/EU when solvent consumption exceeds 1 t/year. Waste oils, bilge water, and salvage debris must be transferred exclusively to licensed waste collectors using applicable EWC codes and hazardous waste consignment notes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) workplace registration and health and safety inspection certificate for any non-seagoing employees; fire safety attestation from the Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours for occupied premises; municipal structural load clearance for any workshop or storage facility; seagoing staff must hold Luxembourg maritime medical fitness certificates and STCW-compliant qualifications.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct corporate taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for Luxembourg VAT; central e-Government filing portal: myguichet.lu; direct tax e-filing: e-Tax (ACD); VAT e-filing: eTVA (AEDT).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg SARL with foreign shareholders: (1) incorporate before a Luxembourg notary and register with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) to obtain the national business number (matricule). (2) If taxable supplies are made in Luxembourg, register for VAT with the AEDT via the standard VAT registration application filed through myguichet.lu; the AEDT issues the Luxembourg VAT ID (TVA). (3) A non-established foreign entity making taxable supplies in Luxembourg must appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative, jointly and severally liable for VAT, pursuant to Art. 61 of the Luxembourg VAT Law. (4) Any permanent establishment created in Luxembourg also requires separate RCS registration and the corresponding ACD tax number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An SARL is a resident capital company and may not elect partnership pass-through status; Luxembourg does not provide a check-the-box regime. Available elections include: VAT fiscal unity (Art. 60 VAT Law) for closely related persons; urban income tax / CIT fiscal integration under Art. 164bis LIR; exemption of small enterprises from VAT (Art. 57 VAT Law) where the annual turnover threshold is met; and the participation exemption regime (Art. 166 LIR) for qualifying shareholdings. Hybrid mismatch and ATAD rules apply by statutory operation rather than elective check-the-box.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA – Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée), governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979, as amended, and Council Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold for non-established foreign entities; VAT registration is compulsory before the first taxable supply in Luxembourg. Domestic small enterprises may apply for a VAT exemption franchise under Art. 57 VAT Law where annual turnover does not exceed EUR 35,000 (VAT-exclusive).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently impose mandatory B2B e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, SAF-T continuous transaction controls, or digital stamping. B2G e-invoicing is mandatory for invoices to Luxembourg central public-sector bodies through the PEPPOL BIS 3.0 network. Standard VAT invoice rules continue to apply and no API-based clearance or digital stamping is in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% VAT applies to goods dispatched or transported to a destination outside the EU (Art. 41 VAT Law / Art. 146 EU VAT Directive), supported by documentary proof of removal. Services: offshore towage and salvage services qualify for 0% VAT under Art. 43 Luxembourg VAT Law / Art. 148 EU VAT Directive where such services are supplied directly for the needs of qualifying sea-going vessels used in international or high-seas navigation, or for their equipment, cargo or crew. The direct-needs requirement and the vessel's international-navigation status must be contractually evidenced; zero-rating is not automatic for services supplied to non-vessel owners or for shore-side services later time-chartered.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (SAD) accepted by Luxembourg or relevant EU customs authorities
Bill of lading / sea-waybill or equivalent transport document showing departure from EU customs territory
Commercial invoice and the underlying towage, salvage, or affreightment contract (e.g., Lloyd's Open Form)
Proof of payment and inward remittance certificate (bank SWIFT MT103 or equivalent evidence of hard currency repatriation)
Ship registry certificate or declaration by the vessel owner confirming international navigation (e.g., trading outside EU waters)
Vessel logbook, port call itinerary, or GPS/route documentation evidencing actual deep-sea use
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and ACD may jointly audit export zero-rating claims and require full documentary substantiation within the statutory retention period. If zero-rating is denied or unsupported, VAT is reassessed at the standard rate of 17% together with delay interest; administrative fines of 50% up to 200% of the evaded tax may be imposed, with higher penalties for intentional fraud; Luxembourg criminal sanctions may include imprisonment. Input VAT already claimed or refunded in respect of the zero-rated export is clawed back with statutory interest, fresh export refunds are suspended, and the limitation period is extended to 10 years in fraudulent cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) – Luxembourg Monetary Institute and member of the Eurosystem; foreign exchange policy competence resides with the European Central Bank (ECB) within the euro area framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. Luxembourg applies EU capital movement liberalisation under Articles 63–66 TFEU with no general exchange control restrictions. Profit remittance is unrestricted for non-resident shareholders, subject only to standard corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICB), and net wealth tax (IFI) compliance, plus withholding tax on dividends (15% standard, reduced under tax treaties or the parent-subsidiary directive). No prior BCL authorisation is required for dividend distributions where the SARL's net assets remain above the minimum share capital threshold (€12,370 for a standard SARL).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export proceeds surrender obligation exists in Luxembourg. Invoices billed in EUR or foreign currency for offshore towing and salvage services may be held freely onshore or offshore. However, the BCL requires statistical reporting of cross-border payments in excess of €12,500 per transaction under Regulation BCE/2013/33 and BCL Circular 2011/240, for balance-of-payments statistical purposes only; this does not constitute a repatriation or conversion mandate.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR current account for towage disbursements) + Escrow Account for salvage contract deposits
Operational Account with export trade settlement facilities (MT103, SWIFT corporate access) and FX hedging line
Operational Account and dedicated Escrow Safekeeping Account for Lloyds Open Form (LOF) security deposits
Operational Account for large-ticket salvage working capital; Capital Escrow Account for vessel asset acquisitions
Operational Account with integrated trade finance and standby letter of credit (SBLC) desk

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low for primary treasury use; acceptable only as secondary payment aggregation rails. Luxembourg-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) under CSSF supervision (e.g., emerchantpay, Satispay-style operators) may hold e-money and process disbursements, but the CSSF requires such institutions to escrow client funds in a segregated account at a credit institution. Offshore EMIs (UK FCA or Lithuania LB regulated) are legally usable for ancillary EUR collections under EU passporting, but their credit-rating and weak custody protections make them unsuitable as primary clearing rails for salvage contract deposits and LOF security. Due to the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML classification of ISIC 5222, the CSSF-regulated banks will likely reject offshore EMI-sourced funds for the first 12 months of the banking relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is mandatory only for individuals acting as directors or beneficial owners. The statutary manager (gérant) of a Luxembourg SARL, if an individual, must appear in person at the bank's Luxembourg branch for the initial KYC interview. Legal entity directors may be attested remotely, but the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) must be identified through the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (REBECO) with a certified extract. Remote onboarding is permitted for non-face-to-face parts where the bank applies enhanced video-identification under CSSF prudential standards, but a face-to-face meeting at the BCL-licensed bank's premises is near-universal practice for marine services companies with a fallback of a sworn notary attestation in the director's country of residence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk maritime sector flag: ISIC 5222 (offshore towage/salvage) may involve salvage rewards, wreck removal, and emergency towing payments from shipowners, insurers, or P&I clubs, presenting sanctions and terrorist-financing exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Fully executed Lloyds Open Form (LOF 2020) arbitration clause and Standard Form Towage Agreement; (2) International Salvage Union membership certificate; (3) ISPS Code security compliance certificate for vessels; (4) IMO Company Identification Number and MMSI registry extracts; (5) Consolidated sanctions screening policy (EU Regulation 765/2006 Ukraine, EU 267/2012 Iran, OFAC SDN match protocol); (6) 36 months of client and counterparty due diligence records including P&I club confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Escrow account concentration trigger: Salvage awards and towage prepayments may exceed €500,000 per transaction, triggering enhanced source-of-wealth review of the payor (often a foreign insurer or shipowner).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Original marine insurance certificates backing the payment; (2) Correspondent bank SWIFT MT103 chain from the paying insurer's clearing bank; (3) Salvage security bond (LOF security) issued by the P&I club; (4) Independent legal opinion confirming the commercial purpose of the funds transfer; (5) Signed towage service agreement with explicit disbursement schedule; (6) Evidence of no politically exposed person (PEP) involvement in the counterparty shareholding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: A Luxembourg SARL served by a foreign-director structure or complex corporate chain above it may trigger refusal under CSSF anti-money laundering law (Loi du 12 novembre 2004, as amended).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Certified REBECO registration extract showing all natural person UBOs above the 25% threshold; (2) Organisational chart with all intermediate holding entities, certified by a Luxembourg notary; (3) Audited financial statements of all intermediate companies (last 3 years); (4) Beneficial owner declarations executed under penalty of perjury; (5) Tax residency certificates (form 3-EG) for all corporate shareholders.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injection from a non-EU parent must be paid by SWIFT MT103 to the SARL's BCL-licensed bank account with the purpose code under EU BOP Statistics classification 'S.12' (other investment) or Code 22 (equity capital contribution), with the free-text field stating 'Apport en capital – SARL Luxembourg, augmentation de capital social'. Verification requires: attribution of the funds to the SARL's notarised articles of association and the BCL statistical survey declaration (collecte BCL) where the transaction exceeds €12,500. Where the capital injection exceeds €20 million, ECB notification is required under Regulation (EU) No 1333/2014 on balance-of-payments statistics, but no prior approval is needed. Routing must avoid so-called 'shell-company banking' red flags: the remitter must be a bank-account holder, not an anonymous intermediary, and the SARL must receive the funds in the same name as reflected in its registration certificate (extrait du RCS).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Salvage and towage trade settlements should be cleared via SWIFT MT103 on a standard 'our cost' basis for sub-threshold disbursements, and via irrevocable documentary credit (Commercial LC, UCP 600) for vessel purchase, bunkering, or sub-contract salvage payments above €250,000. For emergency salvage operations, the target rails are Lloyds Standard Form Wire Credits via the Lloyd's Salvage Branch and P&I club security providers, using ISO 20022 pain.001/camt.103 messages for corporate-to-bank initiation. The FX leg (where subcontractors invoice in USD, GBP, or NOK) must use covered SPOT FX executed via the bank's electronic FX portal with deal ticket capture to satisfy CSSF best-execution under MiFID II. No EU capital controls or border taxes apply to these outbound wires, but the bank will apply a beneficiary bank sanctions screen on all counterparties in high-seas territories.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forward (standard, up to 24-month tenor) – EUR/USD and EUR/GBP hedging for salvage awards denominated in non-EUR currencies

Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) – permissible solely for emerging-market currency exposures that are non-convertible onshore (e.g., counterparties in USD-pegged jurisdictions or salvage claims against flag states outside the EEA), run through a BCL-regulated bank on a deliverable-into-EUR basis

Cross-Currency Swap (EUR-USD) – permissible for long-term towage contracts > 12 months where the debt service or capital expenditure is USD-denominated; must be novated to a clearing house where Bilateral Margin Rules under EMIR apply
Foreign Exchange Option (EUR call / USD put) – permissible for tender-stage salvage contracts with conditional cash flows, subject to the bank's master ISDA and CSA documentation
ERM2-compatible spot and forward EUR/CHF lines – peripheral, used only for Swiss consortium subcontractor settlements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year; amendments reflecting share transfers within one month of knowledge
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine of EUR 1,250 to EUR 25,000; adverse publication of persistent non-compliance; failure does not itself trigger administrative strike-off but combined with missing annual accounts may support RCS removal proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) and filing documentation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS/LBR) via eJustice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months of the balance-sheet date; calendar-year entities by 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal RCS notice after the seven-month window; coercive astreinte of up to EUR 250 per day by court order; criminal sanctions for directors; administrative strike-off (radiation) may be commenced after two consecutive years of default, preceded by RESA publication notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (déclaration d'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May of the year following the taxable year; automatically extended to 31 December if filed by a Luxembourg-approved tax adviser
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 0.3% per month on late tax; administrative fines for late filing up to EUR 25,000; tax assessment by estimation; no immediate administrative strike-off unless combined with non-filing of accounts and RCS default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal business tax return (impôt commercial communal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) in coordination with the commune of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May of the year following the taxable year; extension to 31 December with an approved tax adviser
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Same fiscal penalty regime as CIT: default interest at 0.3% per month, fines up to EUR 25,000 and estimated assessment; no direct strike-off trigger.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net wealth tax return (impôt sur la fortune) and annual minimum net wealth tax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May of the year following the taxable year; extension to 31 December with an approved tax adviser
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 0.3% per month; late filing fines up to EUR 25,000; enforced recovery and attachment of corporate assets; no automatic administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL must appoint an independent statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) where, on the balance-sheet date, it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average headcount 50 employees. Audit is also compulsory for regulated financial institutions, insurance and reinsurance undertakings, and for companies preparing consolidated financial statements under IFRS.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002 transposing EU accounting directives) for individual accounts of the SARL; EU-adopted IFRS for listed companies and consolidated financial statements; optional IFRS for certain unlisted groups under the supervision of ACD.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every Luxembourg entity must confirm its beneficial ownership data in the RBE annually, by 31 March at the latest. For share transfers resulting in a UBO change, the updated confirmation is due within one month of the change being recorded. The annual confirmation must be accompanied by no fee and must certify current UBO details.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,200 - USD 7,500 per annum for third-party registered office and corporate agent services in Luxembourg City
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 18,000 per annum depending on balance-sheet complexity and statutory-audit trigger

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined Luxembourg City marginal rate (base CIT 17% + unemployment fund surcharge 1.19% + municipal business tax 6.75%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption: 100% exemption of qualifying dividends and capital gains (participation >=10% or acquisition cost >=EUR 1.2m, 12-month holding period); IP Box: 80% exemption of qualifying IP income resulting in approximately 5% effective rate; Net Wealth Tax: 0.5% annual levy with EUR 3,550 minimum for SARL
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward with no statutory time limit; annual utilization capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 70% of taxable income exceeding EUR 1,000,000 (effective from 1 January 2017)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 520 (Corporate Income Tax Return) with Form 530 (Municipal Business Tax) and Form 540 (Net Wealth Tax) annexes; e-filing via MyGuichet.lu portal of the Administration des Contributions Directes
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending 31 December (calendar year), the return for tax year N is due by 31 December of year N+1; for non-calendar fiscal years, due by 31 December of the year following the fiscal year end; newly incorporated SARLs must file within their first fiscal year even if accounts are not yet closed

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: legal name, registered office, Luxembourg national tax number (NIF) and RCS registration number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the full Luxembourg registered address, all directors and managers, and identify the Luxembourg permanent representative for tax purposes

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable period: calendar year or statutory financial year start and end dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For short first accounting period, state the exact opening and closing dates approved by the shareholders

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial profit or loss per the audited annual accounts before corporate tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the Luxembourg GAAP profit and loss statement; non-resident managed SARLs must ensure the accounts reflect actual offshore towage and salvage revenue

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Extra-accounting additions: non-deductible expenses such as excessive management fees, non-deductible VAT, penalties, and disallowed entertainment expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose intra-group management fees separately with an arm's length justification; persistent overstatement is a fatal audit trigger

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and tax-exempt income: participation exemption dividends, 80% IP exempt income, and other non-taxable items
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must document the 12-month holding period and 10% participation threshold to substantiate the exemption claim

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax (CIT) taxable basis before loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute in EUR; any cross-border recharges must be consistent with the transfer pricing documentation held by the SARL

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year loss offset applied within the EUR 1,000,000 plus 70% of excess taxable income ceiling
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss certificates and tax assessments for prior years must be retained to support each utilization

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal Business Tax (communal trade tax) computation and commune rate applied
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the place of effective management for apportionment; a Luxembourg OPC (offshore operational company) must have its business offices in Luxembourg to claim the lower commune rates correctly

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net Wealth Tax computation: net asset value as of 1 January of the tax year at 0.5%, subject to minimum
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident shareholders, the net wealth tax applies to Luxembourg situs assets including registered towage vessels and contractual receivables

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing annex: disclosure of all cross-border related-party transactions (towage charter hire, salvage fees, management fees, intercompany funding)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the TP method applied for each transaction and reference the contemporaneous Local File; failure to complete this annex requests a 45-day ACD documentation summons

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: DAC6 and GAAR disclosure of reportable cross-border arrangements involving the Luxembourg entity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident promoters and intermediaries should verify their Luxembourg DAC6 filing obligations before the distribution structure is executed

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing triggers a formal reminder, ex officio assessment, administrative fine up to EUR 25,000, late-payment interest at 0.8% per month on any due tax, an additional 10% tax increase for non-payment by the statutory due date, and forfeiture of the loss-carryforward utilization for the delayed period

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic Luxembourg dividend withholding tax; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying corporate shareholders holding at least 10% for an uninterrupted 12-month period (refund available if the 12-month condition is fulfilled after distribution); reduced rates from 0% to 15% under applicable double tax treaties
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must be the beneficial owner and provide (i) a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the residence country's tax authority, (ii) a declaration of beneficial ownership to the Luxembourg paying agent, and (iii) for EU resident parents, a commitment to the 12-month holding requirement. The paying agent submits the file to the Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for relief at source; alternatively, relief is obtained by filing a Luxembourg refund claim within five years of the distribution date
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% Luxembourg domestic withholding tax on outbound royalties and debt interest (no statutory or treaty withholding for non-residents); however, anti-hybrid, BEPS and economic substance rules may recharacterize excessive royalty or interest payments as constructive dividends subject to the 15% withholding tax

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 750,000,000 consolidated annual group turnover threshold for mandatory Master File and Country-by-Country Report; Local File and supporting TP documentation must be prepared where cross-border related-party transactions (towage charter hire, salvage fees, management fees, intercompany financing) exist, irrespective of size, and produced to the ACD within 45 days of audit request
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not enact a standalone Economic Substance Regulations statute (as in BVI/Cayman), but the domestic GAAR (Article 6 LIR), ATAD rules and CJEU jurisprudence impose a substantive economic substance test: the SARL must have a physical office, operative employees, locally taken management decisions and genuine offshore towage/salvage activity to benefit from treaty relief, the participation exemption and the 0% parent-subsidiary dividend WHT. Artificial letterbox arrangements are disregarded and recharacterized

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful submission of false Form 520 declarations, concealment of offshore salvage contract income, artificial invoicing of towage services, or destruction of accounting records of the Luxembourg SARL
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of all evaded taxes plus 0.8% monthly late interest, administrative penalty up to EUR 25,000, criminal fine up to EUR 25,000 and/or imprisonment up to five years under the General Tax Law (AO sections 396-399), publication of conviction, and loss of professional licenses for maritime towage and salvage
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers who order or knowingly accept the false filing are jointly and severally liable for the tax deficiency; criminal courts may order restitution of personal assets, travel bans, prohibition from managing commercial entities, and imprisonment up to five years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A Luxembourg SARL that operates as a pure mailbox: no physical office, no employees, no towage or salvage operations conducted from Luxembourg, no local decision-making, and no commercial purpose other than exploiting the participation exemption and the DTA network
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD disallows the participation exemption and treaty benefits, recharacterizes intercompany cash flows as constructive dividends, imposes the full 24.94% combined CIT plus 0.8% monthly interest and an administrative penalty up to EUR 25,000; in cases of intentional abuse, criminal tax fraud sanctions may be added
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face civil liability for the unpaid tax under the unlawful distribution doctrine of Luxembourg Company Law, travel bans in cross-border investigations, and criminal sanctions if the artificial arrangement was knowingly structured

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or produce the Local File and TP documentation within 45 days of an ACD request, or absence of an arm's length benchmark for intercompany salvage, towage or management fees charged to related offshore entities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Ex officio upward TP adjustment of the Luxembourg taxable profit, recharacterization of undisclosed intra-group transactions, 0.8% monthly late interest, administrative fine up to EUR 25,000 for missing documentation, and double taxation exposure without MAP relief
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally assessed for the unpaid tax and interest if the omission resulted from fraud or gross negligence; deliberate TP fraud escalates to criminal tax evasion liability with potential imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering and Beneficial Ownership Violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting Lloyd's Standard Form wire payments or escrow settlements without customer due diligence under AMLD5/AMLD6, failing to register the ultimate beneficial owners in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), or executing towage/salvage payments that conceal sanctioned or criminal cargo interests
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CSSF and ACD administrative fines up to EUR 1,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover; criminal AML penalties of imprisonment up to five years and fines up to EUR 5,000,000; RBE registration violations carry criminal fines up to EUR 250,000; escrow accounts may be frozen by the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly facilitate maritime salvage money laundering are criminally liable, with seizure of personal assets, travel bans, withdrawal of the towage operating license, and imprisonment up to five years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful Dividend Repatriation and WHT Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits to a foreign shareholder without withholding the statutory 15% dividend tax, using forged or invalid Tax Residence Certificates to claim 0% DTA or Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, or disguising dividend distributions as management fees to avoid withholding tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The full 15% dividend WHT becomes immediately recoverable from the withholding agent, plus 0.8% monthly late interest and a 10% additional tax penalty; criminal fine up to EUR 25,000 or imprisonment if intent is proven
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Withholding agent liability is extended personally to directors who authorized the unlawful distribution; they face civil recovery, travel bans, personal bankruptcy exposure and imprisonment for deliberate WHT evasion
